narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Two hundred forty divided by five is forty eight millilitres of acid.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The five belongs to water, and the acid is one part out of six.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Dividing by one term alone breaks the ratio, so that slip is wrong.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 240 ÷ 5 = 48 mL of acid; the bottle splits into 1 part acid and 5 parts water; the bubble is struck in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>To check, add the two amounts, and you must get back two hundred forty.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Then forty to two hundred must simplify to one to five.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the bottle; two check lines appear: 40 + 200 = 240; 40 : 200 = 1 : 5

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu divides two hundred forty by five and says forty eight millilitres of acid. The five belongs to water, and the whole has six parts, so the bubble is struck.
